deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'tame' (modéré) category. Its objects are tame subsets of the R^n, with axioms M1–M8; R_0 is apparently a distinguished set of admissible point-values. The previous page introduced two axioms. (M6): every tame subspace Z ⊂ X is a finite intersection of fibres f_α^{-1}(e_α) of tame functions with e_α ∈ R_0, and the f_α separate the points of X∖Z. Equivalently, the contraction X/Z exists strictly, i.e. compatibly with the underlying-set functor. (M7) is a tame Tietze extension axiom: tame functions on Z extend to X. He then stated a proposition: under M5–M7, amalgamated sums X_1 ⊔_Z X_2 along embeddings Z ↪ X_i exist and commute with the forgetful functors. This page is the proof.

Proof. Choose a tame embedding Z ⊂ R^I. By M7, extend its coordinate functions to tame maps u_i : X_i → R^I (i = 1, 2). By M6, choose tame maps X_i → R^{A_i} that are constant equal to e_i ∈ R_0^{A_i} on Z, have fibre exactly Z over e_i, and separate the points of X_i∖Z. Thus they realise a tame embedding of X_i/Z_i, with Z_i = u_i(Z).

The combined map X_1 → R^{I ⊔ A_1} = R^I × R^{A_1} is then injective:
- points of Z are separated by u_1;
- points off Z are separated by the f_α;
- a point of Z and a point off Z differ in the second factor.
He calls this map an embedding, and the square with Z = X_1 ∩ (R^I × {e_1}) is cartesian. The same holds for X_2.

Next he places both in one ambient space: X_1 ↪ R^I × R^{A_1} × {e_2} and X_2 ↪ R^I × {e_1} × R^{A_2}, both inside R^{I ⊔ A_1 ⊔ A_2]. The two linear slices meet in R^I × {e_1} × {e_2}, and X_1 ∩ X_2 = Z there. This is diagram (*), a cube-like diagram of cartesian squares. The (implicit) conclusion is that the union X_1 ∪ X_2 ⊂ R^{I ⊔ A_1 ⊔ A_2} realises the pushout X_1 ⊔_Z X_2.

Why the union is the pushout:
- Each X_i is the trace of the union on a closed linear slice (e.g. X_2 ∩ (R^I × R^{A_1} × {e_2}) = Z ⊂ X_1). So both pieces are closed in the union.
- Hence the induced topology is the pushout topology, and the underlying set is the set-theoretic pushout.

The purpose is to show that the axiomatically defined category of tame spaces is closed under gluing along subspaces. This feeds the next page, on ind-tame spaces with finite limits and sums.
errors: Gap: injectivity of X_1 → R^I × R^{A_1} is asserted to give a 'plongement' (an embedding in the tame category, i.e. an isomorphism onto a tame image). That needs an axiom saying that injective tame maps are embeddings, or a separate argument; this is not spelled out on the page.

The final step is not written: that X_1 ∪ X_2 is tame (stability under finite unions) and that a map out of it is tame when its restrictions to X_1 and X_2 are (a gluing property, needing the closedness of the slices and of Z). This is left implicit.

Strictly, M7 is needed in a vector-valued form: extending the map Z → R^I coordinatewise. That is fine. However, e_i ∈ R_0 is used so that {e_i} is a tame point; the role of R_0 is not explained here.
Minor notational slip: Z_i = u_i(Z) is written although u_i restricted to Z is just the given embedding; presumably the image of Z in X_i is meant.

ideas.what: Realising the pushout X_1 ⊔_Z X_2 of tame (definable) sets as an affine tame set. Extend the embedding of Z by Tietze extension, add the 'collapsing' coordinates that embed X_i/Z, and place the X_i in transverse slices R^I×R^{A_1}×{e_2} and R^I×{e_1}×R^{A_2}.
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / pushouts of definable (semialgebraic, o-minimal) sets along closed definable subsets; affineness of glued definable spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic spaces, early 1980s); Robson, 'Embedding semi-algebraic spaces' (1983); van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures (1998), ch. 10
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for an axiomatic tame topology with such stability properties, without this construction

ideas.what: Axiomatic approach: deriving existence of strict amalgamated sums from just two axioms. These are 'closed subsets are fibres of finitely many tame functions separating points off Z' (M6) and 'tame Tietze extension' (M7).
ideas.modern_name: Definable zero-set property plus definable Tietze extension theorem in o-minimal expansions of fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimal Tietze extension, 1980s–1998); Knebusch/Delfs in the semialgebraic case

missed.claim: An early (1970s) axiomatic proof that tame categories satisfying M6 + M7 have pushouts along embeddings that commute with forgetful functors. It is realised affinely by a slice construction in R^{I⊔A_1⊔A_2}. The content later appears independently in semialgebraic and o-minimal geometry. Grothendieck's version is notable mainly as an axiomatic precursor, not as a new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme had worked-out categorical constructions (gluing, quotients) predating o-minimality. Mathematically it is subsumed by van den Dries ch. 10 and the Delfs–Knebusch theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, fairly routine gluing construction. It is now standard in semialgebraic and o-minimal geometry (Tietze extension plus slice embedding). Its interest is chronological and axiomatic (pre-o-minimal, in Grothendieck's own axiom system), not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'On peut (par M f)' should read 'On peut (par M7)', i.e. the Tietze-type extension axiom.
'comme des Mb' should read 'comme dans M6' or 'comme des M6': the maps are provided by axiom M6.
'Z_i' is underlined in the image, with '= u_i(Z)' written beneath it.
'e_1 ∈ R^{A_1}_0' is correct: the point lies in R_0^{A_1}.
In the struck-out first version of diagram (*), the bottom right reads approximately 'R^I × R_1^{A_1} × R^{A_2}' (crossed out), and the bottom-left arrow is Z → R^I×{e_1}×{e_2}.
In the final diagram (*), the bottom-left letter is an overwritten Z, with a long arrow Z ↪ X_2 and X_2 sitting under R^I×{e_1}×R^{A_2}. There is a vertical arrow from Z up to X_1 on the left.
